user.title: VoiceBM
user.description: VoiceBM adds local speaker identity to your voice pipeline. Pick the speech-to-text engine it should transcribe with — normally your existing Whisper. VoiceBM identifies the speaker on the same audio and publishes it for JARVIS / Ollama, while your Whisper does the transcription.

abort.no_backend_stt: No speech-to-text engine was found to transcribe with. Set up your Whisper add-on/integration first, then add VoiceBM.

data.identity_inject: Inject the identified name into the transcript
data.identity_wait_ms: Max wait for the identity verdict (ms, only if injecting)
data.share_dir: Shared audio folder (both HA and the VoiceBM add-on must see this)
data.gallery_dir: Speaker gallery folder (where the engine stores enrolled voices; default /share/voicebm)

engine_addon_missing.title: VoiceBM engine add-on not installed
engine_addon_missing.description: Speaker identity needs the VoiceBM engine add-on (it runs the voice-biometrics ML that cannot run inside Home Assistant Core). Copy the package's addon-voicebm folder into /addons on your system, then Settings > Add-ons > Add-on Store > (menu) > Check for updates, and install VoiceBM from Local add-ons. The integration will configure and start it automatically. Transcription keeps working in the meantime.
